This yields an Ehrenfest-like hierarchy of Hopf singularities, in which the first nonanalytic derivative is determined by the lowest-order coupling between the observable and the limit-cycle waveform that survives phase averaging. The time averages of generic observables therefore exhibit kink singularities, while symmetry or geometric cancellations can suppress lower-order couplings and shift nonanalyticity to higher derivatives. We demonstrate this mechanism in chemical, electronic, and climate oscillators. Our results identify supercritical Hopf bifurcations as a universal mechanism for nonanalytic observable behavior, where singular yet non-diverging features emerge without any underlying singular stationary state.
item.dc:creator: Benedikt Remlein, Massimiliano Esposito

item.title: AI estimation of partition functions with the PULSE method for the thermodynamic properties of disordered compounds
item.description: arXiv:2605.28594v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Predicting the thermodynamic properties of chemically disordered materials is constrained by the combinatorial growth of possible atomic configurations, which makes conventional sampling approaches computationally costly. In this work, we extend the PULSE (Partition function Unsupervised Learning Sampling and Evaluation) approach that enables the estimation of observable-dependent partition functions, thereby extending its applicability from local atomic quantities to general thermodynamic observables. This is based on a generative machine-learning approach in which a single model both generates statistically representative atomic configurations and provides explicit partition function estimates. Our primary goal is to assess it on the two-dimensional Ising model, an exactly solvable benchmark system sharing the same statistical-mechanical formulation as chemically disordered binary materials, and compare its performance against exact brute-force calculations as well as Wolff and Wang-Landau Monte Carlo algorithms. PULSE reproduces the relevant partition functions accurately using a limited number of configurations, at a sampling cost that does not grow with system size. These key results demonstrate the relevance of our method to enable the study of disordered materials at scales that are difficult to achieve using conventional approaches, and with limited computational effort.
item.dc:creator: Baptiste Bernard, Luca Messina, Eiji Kawasaki, Emeric Bourasseau

item.title: Diffusion-Driven Surface Autocatalysis in Exterior Domains
item.description: arXiv:2606.14133v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the collective dynamics of independent particles that diffuse outside a spherical surface, on which they are replicated with a prescribed catalytic rate. In spatial dimensions three and higher, the transient nature of diffusion creates a competition between autocatalytic branching and escape to infinity, leading to three distinct regimes: subcritical (finite limiting population), critical (algebraic growth), and supercritical (exponential growth). The rotational symmetry of the domain and an explicit form of the single-particle diffusion propagator allow us to fully investigate the time evolution of the population size, including the mean population size, variance, higher-order moments, as well as the whole distribution. In particular, we obtain an explicit form of the distribution at long times and describe a slow, power-law approach to this steady-state limit. We further extend the steady-state analysis to general exterior domains using the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, which determines the critical catalytic rate and reveals how boundary geometry affects the population-size distribution.
item.dc:creator: Denis S. Grebenkov

item.title: Renormalization-Group Fixed Points Not Associated with Universality Classes
item.description: arXiv:2609.18984v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Universality classes have recently been identified for self-similar solutions of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) as consequences of repeated renormalization-group (RG) transformations that eliminate irrelevant structures. Whether all RG fixed points are associated with universality classes, however, remains unclear. We address this question by extending a recently proposed predictive RG framework to traveling-wave solutions, using the Burgers and Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equations as examples. Traveling waves can be mapped onto self-similar forms via a logarithmic transformation. Applying the predictive RG to the log-transformed governing equations yields an RG-flow analysis that reproduces shock and soliton solutions, thereby identifying traveling waves as RG fixed points and the logarithmic variable as RG-flow time. Although the predictive RG framework has shown that self-similar fixed points are associated with universality classes, we find that the present traveling-wave fixed points do not produce the irrelevant structures whose elimination normally gives rise to universality classes. This failure originates from the logarithmic representation, which renders analytic local functions of the field and its derivatives scale invariant, thereby preventing the emergence of irrelevant structures. Traveling waves thus provide explicit examples of RG fixed points without universality classes. These observations suggest that the absence of universality classes may be generic for traveling-wave RG fixed points formulated through logarithmic coordinates. The absence of universality classes suggests that information associated with initial conditions may persist asymptotically, promoting memory retention. The Burgers and KdV examples suggest that memory of initial conditions can survive RG transformations, although its form remains system dependent.
item.dc:creator: Ko Okumura

item.title: Intermittency in Wind-Driven Fires
item.description: arXiv:2609.22541v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a wind-driven forest-fire model in one dimension in which a fire can jump gaps between trees to ignite disjoint downwind forests. The size of a gap that a fire can jump depends on the fire intensity, which increases as the fire propagates through trees and diminishes as the fire jumps gaps. Trees grow on empty sites at rate $r$ and lightning strikes each site with rate $f$. When $f\ll r/L$, where $L$ is the system length, lightning is sufficiently rare that quasi-deterministic dynamics arises where all trees are consumed when a lightning-induced fire occurs. For $f\gg L^{-\mu}$ with $\mu\approx 0.8$, lightning is sufficiently frequent that a steady state is reached, but with unexpected behaviors for the forest- and gap-size distributions. Intermittency arises in between these regimes, with coexisting temporal domains of deterministic and chaotic dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Laurent H\'ebert-Dufresne, Aanjaneya Kumar, S. Redner

item.title: On thermalization in random free fermions: Statistical origins and energy-dependent ETH structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.01414v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze thermalization and eigenstate thermalization in the random free fermion model, a quadratic Hamiltonian with a Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble hopping matrix, by an exact random-matrix calculation. For a single-particle observable $A$ we compute the ensemble average and fluctuations of $\operatorname{Tr}(A\rho(t))$: we derive the relaxation envelope $g^2(t/\tau_\lambda)$ with $\tau_\lambda = \hbar/(2\eta\sqrt{N})$ and its oscillatory $|t|^{-3}$ tail, both properties of the semicircular limiting density, and we show that the variance of the fluctuations is $O(1/N)$, so that the relaxation profile self-averages at fixed scaled time. Incorporating particle-number conservation, we prove a factorization theorem for the energy-shell statistics of the many-body eigenstates: the energy-independent ETH structure follows from the statistical independence of the eigenvector matrix and the spectrum, and at fixed realization the energy constraint enters only through a covariance subtraction of relative order $1/N$. A controlled eigenvector--eigenvalue correlation deformation $H(\varepsilon)=H_0+\varepsilon H_1$ then generates, at first order in $\varepsilon$, the energy dependence of the diagonal energy-resolved slope and of the off-diagonal spectral function, a single-particle diagnostic of the ETH structure in the allowed particle-hole sector. Correlation-function fluctuations and the single-particle spectral form factor finally identify the subleading $O(1/N)$ late-time fingerprints of two-level spectral correlations. The model thus separates eigenbasis chaos from spectral chaos and identifies the statistical origin of energy-independent versus energy-dependent ETH.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Kan Guo, Zhiqiang Huang

item.title: Nonequilibrium quantum states emerging from flippable spins in random networks
item.description: arXiv:2505.11466v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent advances in programmable quantum simulators have enabled the realization of irregular interaction networks, which natural crystal lattices cannot provide, together with time-resolved observation of quantum many-body dynamics. Understanding the nonequilibrium states that emerge from such networks has only just begun, and whether quantum many-body scar states can emerge in them remains open. Here, focusing on a quantum Ising spin system with random interaction networks under a weak transverse field, we introduce the flippability, the fraction of flippable spins, and present phenomenological laws that predict the emergence of quantum many-body scar states from the network structure. As the flippability increases, the Hilbert space becomes less fragmented. The largest kinetically accessible subspace shows nonintegrable level statistics, yet hosts a few eigenstates with abnormally low participation entropy, signalling scar states. Real-time dynamics from Fock states confirm these signatures: systems with higher flippability tend toward thermalization, whereas a few initial states show anomalously nonthermal dynamics. The flippability thus links the interaction-network structure of the Hamiltonian to nonequilibrium many-body dynamics without translational invariance, and may apply to other kinetically constrained quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiaki Horiike, Yuki Kawaguchi

item.title: The Gamma Expansion of the Level Two Large Deviation Rate Functional for Reversible Diffusion Processes
item.dc:creator: Claudio Landim, Jungkyoung Lee, Mauro Mariani

item.title: Toward a Physics of Deep Learning and Brains
item.description: arXiv:2509.22649v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep neural networks and brains both learn and share superficial similarities: processing nodes are likened to neurons and adjustable weights are likened to modifiable synapses. But can a unified theoretical framework be found to underlie them both? Here we show that the equations used to describe neuronal avalanches in living brains can also be applied to cascades of activity in deep neural networks. These equations are derived from non-equilibrium statistical physics and show that deep neural networks learn best when poised between absorbing and active phases. Because these networks are strongly driven by inputs, however, they do not operate at a true critical point but within a quasi-critical regime -- one that still approximately satisfies crackling noise scaling relations. By training networks with different initializations, we show that maximal susceptibility is a more reliable predictor of learning than proximity to the critical point itself. This provides a blueprint for engineering improved network performance. Finally, using finite-size scaling we identify distinct universality classes, including Barkhausen noise and directed percolation. This theoretical framework demonstrates that universal features are shared by both biological and artificial neural networks.
item.dc:creator: Arsham Ghavasieh, Meritxell Vila-Minana, Akanksha Khurd, John Beggs, Gerardo Ortiz, Santo Fortunato

item.title: Generating function and Bloch representation for quantum Fisher tensor
item.description: arXiv:2511.05260v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Uhlmann relative amplitude between two density matrices is shown to be a generating function, through which the quantum Fisher tensor that contains both the quantum Fisher information matrix and the mean Uhlmann curvature can be obtained via differentiation over system parameters. In the pure state limit, our generating function recovers that of the quantum geometric tensor proposed by Het\'{e}nyi and L\'{e}vay, and also clarifies the fidelity and phase between two quantum states as the generating functions of the quantum metric and Berry curvature, respectively. A generic expression for the quantum Fisher tensor in terms of the Bloch representation of density matrices is derived, which facilitates the calculation of the tensor, mean Uhlmann curvature, and geometric properties derived from the quantum Fisher information matrix. Canonical ensembles of spins are adopted to demonstrate our formalism, which reveals a constant Ricci scalar, a vacuum Einstein equation, and a cosmological constant on the 3D Euclidean manifold of the magnetic field
item.dc:creator: Felipe P. Abreu, Wei Chen

item.title: Invading activity fronts or near-critical clusters may stabilize vulnerable excitable systems against stochastic trajectories terminating in an absorbing state
item.description: arXiv:2511.10807v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stochastic chemical reaction or population dynamics in finite systems often terminates in an absorbing state. Yet in large spatially extended systems, the time to reach the absorbing configuration (e.g., species extinction or fixation) becomes exceedingly long. Tuning control parameters may effectively diminish the survival probability, rendering active states (species coexistence) susceptible to stochastic extinction events. In inhomogeneous settings, where a vulnerable subsystem is diffusively coupled to an adjacent stable patch, the former is re-activated through influx from the interfaces, provided the vulnerable region either sustains spreading activity fronts or near-critical large active clusters. Either dynamical structure resets the system to correlated initial conditions favorable for survival. We demonstrate this generic elimination of finite-size extinction instabilities via immigration flux in stochastic predator-prey, cyclic competition, and epidemic spreading models.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth A. V. Distefano (Virginia Tech), Sara Shabani (Virginia Tech), Uwe C. T\"auber (Virginia Tech)

item.title: Dualities and Topological Classification of the $S=1$ Pyrochlore Spin Ice
item.description: arXiv:2603.03852v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive dual descriptions of the trivial paramagnetic, $\mathbb{Z}_2$-deconfined, and $\mathbb{Z}_2$-confined U(1) Coulomb phases of the $S=1$ pyrochlore spin ice. In the monopole-free limit, the system can be effectively mapped onto 3D $XY$ and Ising loop-gas models depending on the spin anisotropy, which provides theoretical estimates for the phase boundaries, while a macroscopic flux vector classifies the topological sectors via geometric parity rules. Thermal unit monopoles permit endpoints of both directed spin loops and unoriented vacancy loops. The resulting relevant symmetry-breaking fields in the dual $XY$ and Ising descriptions predict rounded crossovers near the monopole-free critical points. Monte Carlo simulations support this monopole-induced rounding.
item.dc:creator: Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, Haruki Watanabe

item.title: Classical Simulability from Operator Entanglement Scaling
item.description: arXiv:2603.05656v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Local-operator entanglement (LOE) quantifies the nonlocal structure of Heisenberg operators and serves as a diagnostic of many-body chaos. We provide rigorous bounds showing when an operator can be well-approximated by a matrix-product operator (MPO), given asymptotic scaling of its LOE $\alpha$-R\'enyi entropies. Specifically, we prove that a volume law scaling for $\alpha\geq 1$ implies that the operator cannot be approximated efficiently as an MPO while faithfully reproducing all expectation values. On the other hand, if we restrict to correlations over a relevant sub-class of (ensembles of) states, then logarithmic scaling of the $\alpha < 1$ entropies implies MPO simulability. This result covers a range of relevant quantities, including infinite temperature autocorrelation functions, out-of-time-ordered correlators, and average-case expectation values over ensembles of computational basis states. Beyond this regime, we provide numerical evidence together with a random matrix model to argue that this simulability result also typically holds for arbitrary states. Our results put on firm footing the heuristic expectation that a low operator entanglement implies efficient tensor network representability, extending celebrated foundational results from the theory of matrix-product states and providing a formal link between quantum chaos and classical simulability.
item.dc:creator: Neil Dowling

item.title: Qudit Implementation of the Rodeo Algorithm for Quantum Spectral Filtering
item.description: arXiv:2603.16049v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Qudits, the multi-level generalization of qubits, provide a natural extension of the binary paradigm in quantum computation and offer new opportunities to enhance algorithmic performance. Beyond their direct applicability to the simulation of multi-level quantum systems, higher-dimensional ancillae can improve sampling efficiency in quantum algorithms by enabling the simultaneous implementation of multiple control operations, thereby reducing circuit complexity. In this work, we pursue three main objectives. First, we present a formulation of the Rodeo algorithm employing a general $d$-level ancilla qudit. Second, we introduce the concept of the \emph{Rodeo kernel}, defined as a two-frequency interferometer, which acts as a spectral filter in the energy domain. Finally, we propose a microcanonical protocol for the Rodeo algorithm. This protocol enables the estimation of entropic quantities through a single energy sweep and admits a natural interpretation as a Gaussian convolution of the density of states. To support the theoretical analysis, we perform numerical evaluations of the corresponding quantum circuit using ancilla qudits of dimensions three, four, and five. The simulations are performed for the one-dimensional Ising model, considering both spin-$\sfrac{1}{2}$ and spin-$1$ particles. The ancilla qutrit implementation exhibits an $18\%$ reduction in fluctuations compared to the qubit implementation. Our results show that qudits provide a framework for spectral analysis and thermodynamic characterization of multi-level quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Julio Cesar Siqueira Rocha, Rodrigo Alves Dias

item.title: Topological Phase Transitions and Their Thermodynamic Fate in Arbitrary-$S$ Classical Pyrochlore Spin Ice
item.description: arXiv:2604.04346v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a self-contained theoretical framework that classifies the topological phases and critical phenomena of classical pyrochlore magnets with arbitrary spin $S$, subject to competing exchange and single-ion anisotropies. We work first in the monopole-free (ice-rule) limit. In the small-$w$ regime, where the single-ion term favors low spin amplitudes, dualities reveal a dichotomy: Integer spins exhibit a continuous 3D $XY$ deconfinement transition, whereas half-integer spins remain in a $U(1)$ Coulomb liquid without any transition. In the large-$w$ regime, where $|S^z| = S$, the macroscopic flux is quantized to multiples of $2S$. Mapping the defect structure to loop gases, we prove that the ice rule is compatible with the modular $\mathbb{Z}_{2S}$ flux conservation at the vertex level if and only if $S \le 3/2$. For $S=3/2$, this maps the system to the three-state Potts model, whose symmetry-allowed cubic invariant drives a first-order transition. For $S \ge 2$, no discrete clock mapping exists; a decomposition of the partition function shows that the only processes sensitive to the discrete $\mathbb{Z}_{2S}$ structure carry exponentially small weight and correspond to irrelevant operators at the 3D $XY$ fixed point, so the deconfinement transition is of the 3D $XY$ type. Finally, incorporating thermal monopoles, we show that they act as a symmetry-breaking effective magnetic field that severs defect strings. Consequently, the continuous transitions are rounded into crossovers, whereas the first-order $S=3/2$ transition is predicted to survive at finite temperatures, terminating at a critical end point. Classical Monte Carlo simulations for $S$ up to $7/2$ corroborate the predicted crossovers at the accessible temperatures, which lie above the estimated critical end point, so the survival of the $S=3/2$ first-order transition remains to be tested directly.
item.dc:creator: Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, Haruki Watanabe

item.title: Opto-criticality in Drude metals near the plasma frequency
item.description: arXiv:2605.08107v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Within a simple unified framework of classical electrodynamics that incorporates background bound charges and currents, we have analytically determined the attenuation constant, phase constant, and reflectivity of Drude metals across the full frequency spectrum ($0 < \omega < \infty$).Our result for reflectivity agrees well with existing experimental data for both plasmas and seawater. Notably, for highly conductive Drude metals ($\omega_p \tau \gg 1$), the attenuation constant simplifies to $k_- \simeq \sqrt{\frac{\mu \epsilon}{2}} \sqrt{\omega_p^2 - \omega^2 + \vert{}\omega_p^2 - \omega^2\vert{}}$ across a broad high-frequency range spanning the plasma frequency $\omega_p$. The branch-point singularity at $\omega=\omega_p$ in this relation reveals opto-critical behavior near $\omega=\omega_p$ in properties such as the attenuation constant, group velocity, and complex dielectric constant, for which we have determined the corresponding opto-critical exponents. Furthermore, we have incorporated quantum corrections into these optical properties via the Drude-Sommerfeld model with Thomas-Fermi screening.
item.dc:creator: Bikram Keshari Behera, Rhitabrata Bhattacharyya, Shyamal Biswas

item.title: Quantum Quenches that Resemble Operator Growth
item.description:
arXiv:2605.23874v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study growth quenches, which are local quenches that may gradually destabilize a false vacuum in certain kinetic constrained quantum lattice models, such as the East-West model. We point out a formal analogy with the dynamics of a local operator in the Heisenberg picture. Exploiting this analogy, we obtain several results on growth quenches by adapting operator-dynamics concepts and methods. First, applying the Krylov approach (recursion method), we conjecture the linear growth of Lanzcos coefficients in generic quenches, $a_m \sim 
u m$ (diagonal), and $b_m \sim \alpha m$ (off-diagonal), extending an operator growth hypothesis. We show that the growth quench dynamics is localized in both Krylov and Fock spaces when $|
u| > 2 \alpha$, and derive a bound for the growth quench analogue of Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_L \le \sqrt{4 \alpha^2 - 
u^2}$ when $|
u| < 2 \alpha$. Second, we realize the Fock localization in large $N$ solvable growth quenches inspired by Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) models. The bound on Lyapunov exponent is saturated in large-$q$ SYK grow quench. By contrast, the growth quench is almost always Fock localized in a nonrandom all-to-all growth quench amenable to semiclassics. Finally, in the 1D East-West model, we interpret Fock space cage states as the existence of a conserved charge. We show that the latter has ballistic transport due to current conservation. Moreover, adding hopping with a fine-tuned amplitude induces a partial localization due to a flat band. Our work suggest growth quenches as a promising approach to realize non-equilibrium coherent phenomena in many-body systems.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Cao

item.title: Tame the Umklapp Processes in Real-Time Lattice Simulation for Hydrodynamics: An Ising Field Theory Study
item.description: arXiv:2606.09984v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We calculate the real-time symmetric correlation function of the stress-energy tensor for a near-integrable Ising field theory consisting of three stable scalar particles via lattice Hamiltonian simulation. Using classical exact diagonalization and the matrix product state tensor network methods, we find that in the scaling region of the lattice theory, Umklapp processes that break continuum momentum conservation are suppressed and the sound modes of relativistic hydrodynamics emerge at long wavelength and late time in non-equilibrium dynamics. The extracted ratio of bulk viscosity to entropy density is $\zeta/s=3.06\pm 0.68$ and the speed of sound is $c_s/c=0.76 \pm 0.02$ at the temperature $T\approx 7.14$ in units of the lowest stable particle's mass. Our study demonstrates the utility of real-time lattice Hamiltonian simulation for describing hydrodynamization and calculating transport coefficients nonperturbatively.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Yao

item.title: Nonlocal Electrostatic Field Theory from Microscopic Description
item.description: arXiv:2607.16429v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The study of electric fields in soft materials converges either to the study of point-like particles (local) in nonlinear theories or to the use of particles with finite sizes in nonlocal linear theories. In this work, we start from the microscopic equations of motion and construct a unified mean field Fokker-Planck equation that describes the non-equilibrium electrostatics of nonlocal nonlinear systems. We obtain a generalized Poisson-Boltzmann equation for such systems, as well as their electrostatic free energy expression. In the linear approximation, we obtain an anisotropic susceptibility in an isotropic fluid, which allows for local linear response inversion in electrostatics.
item.dc:creator: Varazdat Stepanyan, Yevgeni Sh. Mamasakhlisov, Armen E. Allahverdyan

item.title: DSSYK, open ASEP/TASEP and 2d dilaton gravity at strong coupling
item.description: arXiv:2610.01790v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We discuss the triality between stochastic growth models in the KPZ universality class, the DSSYK model, and low dimensional dilaton gravity. The TASEP model, which will be our primary focus, is identified with the strong-coupling limit of two-dimensional quantum gravity. The Hamiltonian of DSSYK and the transfer matrix of ASEP coincide up to an additive constant, and we derive the exact expression for the resolvent of the corresponding transfer matrix in ASEP on a finite interval. We also mention the relation of cumulants with the Tutte polynomial $T(1,q)$ of the crossing graph dual to the chord diagram, which implies the relationship of the models considered with the $Q=0$ Potts model coupled with gravity. We further exploit the realization of all these models in terms of different versions of discrete and continuous random walks on two-dimensional manifolds, which parameterize the Hilbert spaces of the respective theories. The representation of TASEP as the growth model of heaps provides new insight into strong-coupling gravity, suggesting its interpretation as an emerging phenomenon. The new dualities between ASEP and q-TASEP models and heap models providing a useful growth interpretation have been developed.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Gorsky, Elizaveta Kovalenko, Sergei Nechaev

item.title: Uniform Bessel bounds for magnetization crossings in finite Ising chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.06935v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider a finite Ising chain in zero field and ask when the all-up configuration is as likely as zero magnetization (magnetization one for an odd number of spins). For both free and periodic ends, the crossing coupling of a long chain is half the logarithm of its length minus half the logarithm of that logarithm, up to a term that vanishes as the length grows. We compute further terms with explicit constants and, for free ends, bound the crossing at every length. The second term is missing from an earlier approximation and explains why an earlier numerical fit gives a slope below one half. To locate the crossing, we compare the known magnetization law with its Bessel approximation. The Bessel approximation is above the exact weight, and we bound its relative error for every length, coupling and magnetization. At the crossing this bound tends to zero. The central bin still has about as many domain walls as the logarithm of the length on average, so the crossing has a coupling width of order the inverse logarithm. In a fixed positive dimensionless field the last crossing comes from near the edge of the row, at a coupling of about a quarter of the logarithm of the length. For long chains it is the one-spin crossing when the field exceeds half the logarithm of two. Below that value another bin crosses later.
item.dc:creator: Arjun Pemmasani

item.title: Characterizing Fermionic Non-Gaussianity in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model via Replica Twist Entropy
item.description: arXiv:2610.10123v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Understanding the non-equilibrium dynamics of quantum many-body systems plays a central role in modern many-body physics. Intriguing insights emerge from investigating how quantum resources, which are essential for achieving unambiguous quantumness, are generated and spread under chaotic quantum dynamics. In fermionic systems, non-Gaussianity constitutes an important resource beyond entanglement, characterizing the deviation of generic quantum states from free-fermion states. In this Letter, we propose using the \textit{replica twist entropy}, defined through the expectation value of a replica rotation operator with a tunable angle $\alpha$, as a natural probe of non-Gaussianity in pure fermionic states. After deriving its behavior for typical many-body states, we establish a general framework for analyzing the replica twist entropy in solvable Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev models in the large-$N$ limit. Applying this framework to the dynamics of the thermofield double state, we uncover a novel dynamical phase diagram in the parameter space of $\alpha$ and evolution time $t$, exhibiting spontaneous $Z_2$ symmetry breaking at $\alpha=\pi/4$ and universal cusps as a function of $\alpha$ in the long-time regime. Our results pave the way for studying non-Gaussianity in strongly correlated fermionic systems and reveal a new class of dynamical transitions probed by non-Gaussianity.
item.dc:creator: Ning Sun, Pengfei Zhang

item.title: Altermagnetic Control of Charge-4e Superconductivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.13584v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that a two-dimensional classical array of conventional superconducting islands coupled by altermagnetic Josephson junctions supports an independent charge-4e phase. Tuning the altermagnetic splitting suppresses the leading single-pair tunneling harmonic while retaining strong double-pair coupling, producing a finite charge-4e region between staggered and uniform charge-2e states. Using the complete temperature-dependent microscopic Josephson spectrum, we find short-range ordinary pair correlations alongside algebraic coherence of pairs of Cooper pairs. Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless scaling and a half-flux response further identify the charge-4e phase. Our results establish altermagnetism as a microscopic means to select between ordinary and composite superconducting coherence.

item.title: Seismology of Glasses
item.description: arXiv:2610.19602v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Aging and relaxation of glasses proceed through localized rearrangements that also generate long-ranged mechanical responses in their surroundings. We develop a theory that treats these rearrangements as internal microseismic sources, and thereby separates the direct effects emerging from an event from the effects from the far-field displacements it generates. These far-field disturbances propagate and relax through the viscoelastic medium through which they move, producing a stochastic background of weak but numerous perturbations at any given location. Combining the description of local events from the Random First Order Transition theory with this propagating background, we derive a unified equation for the dynamical structure factor of a relaxing glass. The theory identifies a finite wave-vector and time window in which the growing viscoelastic far-field disturbances can produce compressed exponential relaxation, which has been observed using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy. At higher wave vectors that resolve local jumps, heterogeneity of the local event dynamics instead produces stretched exponential relaxation. The crossover between these behaviors depends on the event statistics and the scattering phase accumulated across the region reached through viscoelastic propagation from the numerous distant sources.
